item.content:encoded: This times 1000. If the Hume is arbitrarily defined by just making two universes and setting them as 0 and 100 respectively, then negative and zero Hume levels should be possible. Given the definition of a Hume provided by part 1, then if Humes measured temperature, they would be equivalent to Celsius, even thought this second article treats them like Kelvin most of the time. If Humes were to be treated as an absolute scale (which logically would make more sense), then the lowest theoretical amount of reality possible would need to be used as 0 in Kant Counters and an arbitrarily chosen highest practical application could be used for 100, with special equipment needed to measure levels above 100.

item.title: Re: An Inconsistency
item.content:encoded:
As of yet, no. In nature, the lowest Hume concentrations we've ever encountered have been in the vicinity of ~.27/.28 H; which, while low, is still quite far from an "absolute zero" concentration.

As I see it, this would include the pocket dimension, since even if they never actually physically interacted with it, they would have encountered it.

item.title: Re: An Inconsistency
item.content:encoded: Presumably the .15h is the lowest they’ve managed in this dimension, while 0 is from the pocket dimension.

item.title: An Inconsistency
item.content:encoded:
We created two pocket realities that each contain Scranton Reality Anchors that maintain the Hume levels at an arbitrarily high and low level. These levels have been designated 100 and 0, respectively.

Artificially, we've been able to get concentrations down to .15 H; again, low, but still quite far from that perfect zero. While it is theoretically possible that a zero Hume concentration can exist, it is incredibly unlikely that such a thing can exist naturally in nature or can be artificially created without massive repercussions, as such a thing would not be considered "reality" as we think of (or experience) it.

These pieces of information seem to inherently contradict each other in a way that I'm not sure is intentional. I'm not sure if this is something that can be addressed as a question on the main page, so I'm going to just place it here. If someone wants to pen it in, I'd ask you to place it under Dr. M, but I'd first ask to wait for to Jekeled answer it here/place it in the main article of their own volition.
